s.note: Swiss cheese puffs, warm from the oven.
s.how: Bring the milk, water, butter and a pinch of salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat over the heat until the dough leaves the sides. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy. Beat in most of the Gruyère with the mustard and nutmeg, pipe walnut-sized balls onto lined trays and top with the rest of the cheese. Bake at 200C until puffed and deep golden, without opening the oven. Brush the hot puffs with the truffle oil and scatter with sea salt.

s.note: Lime and avocado with Marie Rose sauce.
s.how: Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, hot sauce and the juice of 1 lime into a pink sauce. Toss the avocado with a squeeze of lime so it stays green. Layer the lettuce and avocado in 4 glasses and pile the prawns on top. Spoon over the sauce, dust with paprika, scatter chives and hang a lime wedge on each glass.

m.note: Garlic butter centre, crisp crumb, buttery mash.
m.how: Mash the butter with the garlic and parsley, roll into a log and freeze until firm. Cut a deep pocket in each breast, push in a slice of the butter and press closed. Dip in flour, egg and panko, then egg and panko again, and chill for 10 minutes. Fry in hot oil until golden all over, then finish in the oven at 200C until cooked through. Meanwhile boil the potatoes and mash with a knob of butter and the milk, and steam the beans. Rest the Kievs for 2 minutes and serve with the mash and beans.

m.note: Crisp-skin snapper over coconut rice with lime.
m.how: Simmer the rice with the coconut milk, 250ml water and a pinch of salt, covered, until tender. Mix the mango, onion, chilli, coriander and the juice of 1 lime for the salsa. Rub the snapper with oil, allspice and salt and cook skin down in a hot pan until crisp, then turn for a minute. Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa piled on top and lime wedges.

w.note: Dark chocolate sponge and fudge icing.
w.how: Whisk the flour, sugar, 60g cocoa and bicarb, then whisk in the eggs, buttermilk, oil and hot coffee to a thin batter. Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 180C until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Melt the chocolate, beat the butter with the icing sugar and remaining cocoa, then beat in the chocolate. Sandwich and cover the cakes with the icing and stand the candles on top.

d.note: Brut, cognac and a bitters-soaked sugar cube. Juno pours champagne holding her Beretta.
d.how: Drop a sugar cube soaked with a few drops of bitters into each chilled flute. Add 15ml cognac, top slowly with champagne and twist a strip of orange peel over each.
